item_title: CoreWeave owed more than $35 billion as of its second-quarter earnings and had $103.7 billion of remaining customer obligations, about 40% of it due in 2028, The Verge reported (Oct 19)
mechanism: CoreWeave borrowed against long customer contracts. With its bonds at distressed spreads, refinancing gets dearer before most of that contracted revenue arrives.

scenarios.direction: Spreads stay wide and CoreWeave leans on its largest customers or Nvidia for funding support instead of new bonds.
scenarios.why: New bonds at about 1,000 basis points over government debt are costly, and three customers supplied almost three-quarters of second-quarter revenue.
scenarios.precedent: In September 2025 CoreWeave disclosed a $6.3 billion order under which Nvidia agreed to buy any cloud capacity CoreWeave could not sell.

scenarios.direction: The stress spreads to other neoclouds and data-centre lenders, raising funding costs across the AI build-out.
scenarios.why: The same day's headlines reported a surge in default-insurance trading on AI debt and fresh highs in tech credit risk, a sector repricing.
scenarios.precedent: In 2001-02 telecom carriers that funded fibre networks with high-yield debt ahead of demand defaulted as spreads widened; Global Crossing filed for bankruptcy in January 2002.

scenarios.direction: Spreads narrow as contracted revenue arrives on schedule and the 2028 payments come to look secure.
scenarios.why: The $103.7 billion is contracted and, per The Verge, cancellable only in very limited circumstances, so the risk is timing more than demand.

context_note: capital-context.yaml (asof 2026-08-25) has no reading for AI-infrastructure credit; it predates the October CoreWeave bond sell-off and should be refreshed.

item_title: CNBC's headline reported France's 10-year bond yield hit 5% for the first time since 2002 amid unrest (Oct 21)
mechanism: A higher French 10-year yield raises France's borrowing cost and lifts the risk premium that euro-area lenders and investors demand on French paper against German bunds.

scenarios.direction: The French premium keeps widening until the European Central Bank signals support for French bonds.
scenarios.why: Unrest that stalls budget repair keeps investors demanding more yield, and the ECB is the only buyer able to cap it quickly.
scenarios.precedent: In July 2012 ECB president Mario Draghi said the bank would do "whatever it takes" for the euro, and Italian and Spanish yields fell in the following months.

scenarios.direction: A political deal on the budget calms the market and yields settle back below 5%.
scenarios.why: The move is tied to unrest and fiscal worry rather than to a change in inflation or growth, so a credible plan removes its cause.
scenarios.precedent: French spreads over bunds widened after the June 2024 snap election was called and then stabilised without central-bank action.

scenarios.direction: The rise spreads to other high-debt euro-area bonds and to global long-end yields, tightening financing for borrowers including AI-infrastructure issuers.
scenarios.why: A repricing of French sovereign risk shifts the benchmark that euro-area corporate credit is priced against.
scenarios.precedent: In September 2022 the UK gilt sell-off forced the Bank of England to buy long-dated gilts.

context_note: capital-context.yaml (asof 2026-08-25) has no euro-area sovereign reading; its cross-border credit reading (BIS bank claims $47.62T, 2026-Q1) is the channel such a shock would use.

item_title: Reuters' headline reported Brent crude hit a five-month high on escalating Middle East conflict (Oct 22)
mechanism: A Brent rise on supply risk to Saudi output lifts inflation expectations and long-end yields, tightening financing for AI-infrastructure borrowers.

scenarios.direction: Brent holds above $100 and inflation expectations rise, pushing central banks toward further tightening.
scenarios.why: Higher fuel costs feed headline inflation, and the snapshot's hawkish Fed hold leaves little room to look through it.
scenarios.precedent: After Russia's February 2022 invasion of Ukraine Brent passed $120 and major central banks raised rates through that year.

scenarios.direction: Spare capacity and stock releases cap the price and it falls back within weeks.
scenarios.why: A spike that does not cut exports for long tends to retrace once supply is seen to be intact.
scenarios.precedent: After the September 2019 Abqaiq attack Brent jumped about 15% in a day and gave the gain back within about two weeks.

scenarios.direction: Oil strength widens the gap between energy producers and AI-heavy equity indexes while the AI trade sells off.
scenarios.why: Same-day headlines tied the Nasdaq decline to both AI doubts and oil, so one shock compounds the other.
scenarios.precedent: In 2022 energy was the best-performing S&P 500 sector while growth technology stocks fell.

context_note: capital-context.yaml (asof 2026-08-25) lists Iran's war, opened 2026-02-28, as its conflict-risk reading and a hawkish Fed hold at 3.50%-3.75% as its rate regime.

item_title: Bloomberg's headline reported AI tech fears pushed global credit spreads to a 17-month high (Oct 23)
mechanism: Wider credit spreads raise the cost of the debt funding AI data-centre buildouts, tightening financing for leveraged borrowers.

scenarios.direction: Spreads keep widening and new issuance by AI-linked borrowers is delayed or repriced.
scenarios.why: Higher spreads cut the return on projects financed with debt and make lenders demand more protection.
scenarios.precedent: In December 2018 US high-yield bond issuance stopped for the month as spreads widened, and it resumed only after the market steadied in early 2019.

scenarios.direction: Spreads narrow again within weeks as equities steady and the AI-financing worries fade.
scenarios.why: A spread spike that does not meet a funding failure tends to retrace once buyers return.
scenarios.precedent: US high-yield spreads peaked in February 2016 during the energy selloff and narrowed over the following months.

scenarios.direction: Stress stays concentrated in AI-linked borrowers while broader credit holds up.
scenarios.why: Same-day headlines tied the pressure to Meta and neocloud financing, not to bank or consumer credit.
scenarios.precedent: In 2015 and 2016 energy bonds repriced sharply while the investment-grade market kept functioning.

context_note: capital-context.yaml (asof 2026-08-25) lists a hawkish Fed hold at 3.50%-3.75% as its rate regime, so higher funding costs meet a central bank with little room to ease.
